Failure analysis · hamster-01 · validation split · 2026-09-17

Where the cut-point model struggles

Model: hamster-01 (3D HAMSTER initialization, RGB + metric depth), the best of the six fine-tunes. Evaluation: 1,358 frames from 4 plants never seen in training; 1,012 with a visible cut, 346 occluded. The task: given the image and a query pixel on the target leaf stalk, return the cut point 10 mm from the stalk's junction with the main stem, or abstain if that region is hidden. Every tile below is a zoom whose window is sized to contain both the label and the prediction.

query pixel (given)label cut point10–20 mm intervaltarget petiole mask (not shown to the model)predictionprediction-to-label distance

Failure gallery: six ways it goes wrong

  1. Background (row 1). The point is placed on the greenhouse rail or far foliage, 0.3 m or more behind the petiole. All of the four worst cases (293–420 px) are this kind, three of them views of one target (seed29/SubStem_41).
  2. Another plant part (row 2). A neighbouring stalk or stem at similar depth, typically where two stalks cross or run parallel.
  3. Near miss on the right stalk (row 3). The commonest outcome: on the correct petiole, 5–25 px from the label. Visually close, but outside the 10–20 mm interval, so useless for a blade.
  4. Wrong abstention (row 4). 31 visible cuts (3%) answered null; thin, backlit stalks and junctions next to fruit.
  5. Fabricated points (row 5). 159 of 346 occluded targets get a point. Only 23 are on the occluder itself (nearer than the petiole by >3 cm); 119 land farther away or on invalid depth, i.e. the model keeps tracing where it thinks the stalk continues.
  6. Hardest target (row 6). seed97/SubStem_50: 34 views, median error 44.8 px, prediction never on the petiole mask. The label geometry checks out (junction visible, parent-stem pixels present, attachment 5 px from the label), so this is a consistent model confusion on one plant structure, not a label error.

Classified by native depth at the predicted pixel versus depth at the query pixel: background = >0.3 m behind, foreground = >0.1 m in front. The important line is the near-miss band: two-thirds of those 5–25 px misses sit beside the 4–5 px-wide stalk on background seen through the foliage. In 2-D they are a few pixels off; in 3-D they are empty air. Only 133 of 981 answers (14%) touch the target petiole at all.

Errors cluster by target, not by view: the same structure is misread from every angle, which is what a model that has memorized 168 training targets does on a new plant.
